title: How Do Interest-Only Mortgages Affect Consumption and Saving over the Life Cycle?
eligible_reason: Single treatment date: interest-only (IO) mortgages were introduced in Denmark in October 2003 for all households (efterIntro = aar > 2003). The DiD compares households with a high pre-introduction illiquid-asset ratio (IAR > 0.5) with low-IAR households, i.e. a two-group, one-date design. No staggered adoption.
design_notes: Danish household-year register panel 2001-2006 (customers of an anonymous mortgage bank merged with Statistics Denmark registers). 2_6_DID.do: treat = high IAR in every pre-2004 year; 1:1 propensity-score/exact matching on 2002 characteristics (psmatch2) with frequency weights; for each age group, reg log_cons_avgperson on treat x efterIntro plus 2002-fixed controls [fweight = freq], vce(robust), no household or year FE. Placebo, stock-participation (probit) and risky-asset-share variants in 2_7-2_9. IO take-up is modelled with probits (2_3, 2_5) and a life-cycle model.
main_or_robustness: main (DiD is one of several analyses; not staggered)
n_adoption_cohorts_note: One introduction date (2003/2004) common to all households.
data_access: proprietary (Statistics Denmark administrative registers via remote access for Danish institutions; pre-2009 mortgage data from an anonymous Danish bank, not accessible)
data_files: Public data.xlsx (aggregate public series for Figures 1, 2, 4 and CPI/house price indices only)
data_files_note: readme.pdf: all micro data and the analysis file Analyse1.dta are confidential and not provided.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text in data/text). Package contents read, no code run.
